newsitem.title: USA: Decision delayed on U.S. West power line capacity.
newsitem.headline: Decision delayed on U.S. West power line capacity.

text.p: A study group convened by the Western Systems Coordinating Council (WSCC) delayed until at least the end of January any decision to raise capacity limits on major western U.S. power lines, sources said Monday.

A spokeswoman for Bonneville Power Administration (BPA), which on Friday presented the group with a proposal to lift line capacity, said the agency was asked to present additional voltage support studies.
"They didn't say yeah or neah. It was kind of discouraging," the spokeswoman said.
The Pacific Intertie lines, which link the Northwest to California, have been capped at near 65 percent of capacity since two massive power blackouts hit the West last summer.
BPA was looking to raise those limits by 25 percent immediately and to full capacity by April, in time for the spring rush of hydroelectric output.

The WSCC study group will meet again with BPA to review the requested studies on January 31. The agency will also meet with a panel of industry experts later this month to examine the voltage support proposals.
